slots.writingObjective: State, as a fact about TextOS's API, that an agent can prepare a CMS draft but a human decision is required to create it.
One sentence for a search result: the three governed effects stay under human review, and an approval is bound to an exact hash and consumed once.
Open on the buyer's worry — an agent with API access writing into a CMS — then say how TextOS's API answered it in September 2026, without listing the mechanism yet.
slots.buyerIntent: Can an agent put unapproved content into my CMS?

slots.heading: What stops an agent from creating an unapproved draft?
slots.writingObjective: Answer directly: which effects require a human decision, that no machine identity can switch that to automatic execution, and that the approval is a single-use grant tied to an exact hash.

slots.heading: Preparing is not doing
slots.writingObjective: Explain the split between the prepare capability (derives the exact action and its hash, no external effect, no credentials hashed) and the create capability, and why draft creation was not relabelled as an internal proposal.
slots.buyerIntent: What can the agent do on its own?

slots.writingObjective: Caption the figure of this note in one factual sentence, grounded in the evidence it cites.

slots.heading: An approval covers exact bytes, once
slots.writingObjective: Tell how the approval is spent: a stale approval fails before the WordPress request when content, TruthCheck lineage or destination changed; a mismatched hash consumes nothing; one grant can back one job only; the grant is claimed, used, then consumed.
slots.buyerIntent: What if the draft changed after I approved it?

slots.heading: Whose name is on the decision
slots.writingObjective: Show that the record keeps the real human who approved, never the machine identity that executed, and that the one ambiguous window — WordPress may have created the draft before TextOS recorded it — stops for reconciliation instead of retrying.
slots.buyerIntent: Who is accountable, and what happens on a crash?

slots.heading: What to ask any AI writing vendor
slots.writingObjective: Give the buyer a short list of questions to put to any vendor, one per sentence, drawn from the mechanisms this note describes. Recommendations only, no claim about TextOS.
